questions.stem: Oxygen is on, but the saturation will not rise. This is most consistent with:

options.text: A simple ventilation problem that always fixes with a higher oxygen flow alone
A shunt, because blood is skipping the air sacs

questions.explanation: In a shunt, blood skips the air sacs, so added oxygen cannot reach it.

questions.stem: After a bronchodilator, the ratio stays at 0.62. This supports:

options.text: A plain film is enough to confirm it
A shunt, because oxygen will not help

questions.explanation: GOLD 2027 confirms COPD with a post-bronchodilator ratio under 0.7.

questions.stem: Both lungs are wet, oxygen is low, and left-atrial pressure is not the cause. This is:
questions.explanation: Acute respiratory distress: wet lungs and low oxygen, and the left atrium is not the cause.

questions.stem: Basal velcro-like crackles and slow scarring, with a quiet exposure history, first suggest:

options.text: Hypersensitivity pneumonitis from a barn or birds

questions.explanation: Idiopathic fibrosis crackles at the bases and may have a quiet history. Hypersensitivity is the place the patient breathes.

questions.stem: A lung disease tightly tied to the place the patient breathes is:
questions.explanation: Ask about the barn, the birds, the hobby.

questions.stem: A malignant pleural effusion should be treated as:

options.text: A simple transudate until proven otherwise
An exudate until the cells say otherwise

questions.explanation: Do not call it a simple transudate and stop looking.

questions.stem: The GOLD 2027 diagnostic cutoff for chronic obstructive pulmonary disease is:

options.text: A saturation that always rises with oxygen

questions.explanation: Post-bronchodilator FEV1/FVC < 0.7 is mandatory to confirm the diagnosis in GOLD 2027.

questions.stem: Helping a patient breathe can fix which problem more readily than a true shunt?

options.text: Blood that never sees the air sacs

questions.explanation: A ventilation problem can improve when you help the patient breathe.

questions.stem: The key distinction of acute respiratory distress versus simple heart-failure fluid is:

options.text: The left atrium is not the cause
The effusion is always a transudate

questions.explanation: The left atrium is not the cause.

options.text: A shunt routes blood past the air sacs, so added oxygen may not raise the saturation.
COPD is confirmed by a post-bronchodilator ratio that stays under 0.7.
A malignant effusion is a simple transudate until proven otherwise.
Hypersensitivity pneumonitis is linked to an inhaled exposure.

questions.explanation: A malignant effusion is an exudate until cytology says otherwise.
